 WASHINGTON (TNND) — First Lady Melania Trump is hosting representatives from Russia and Ukraine at the White House on Thursday, after helping secure a humanitarian ceasefire in the Ukrainian city of Oleshky.
 The White House called the gathering “an extraordinary moment in American history.” It appears to be the first time representatives from both countries have met face-to-face at the White House.
 The Kremlin said Russian President Vladimir Putin’s special envoy Kirill Dmitriev and human rights commissioner Yana Lantratova, who coordinated the ceasefire for Moscow, were expected to attend. Ukraine has not officially confirmed its delegation, but David Arakhamia, who leads President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s party in parliament, will be part of it, his office told NBC News.
 The meeting comes as the Trump administration pushes to end the war. The U.S. is expected to lead renewed trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi, United Arab Emirates, next week.
 The six-day ceasefire began Oct. 27 and ended Nov. 1. It enabled humanitarian aid deliveries and the evacuation of nearly 800 people from Oleshky, where about 2,000 residents had remained amid severe shortages of food and medicine. Ukrainian officials described it as the largest de-escalation effort since Russia’s full-scale invasion in 2022.
 Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy awarded Melania Trump the Order of Princess Olga , first class, on Wednesday, citing her “significant personal contribution to humanitarian support for Ukraine.”
